doc.title: Derek Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995

title: Milt Hinton
summary: Smith praises Milt Hinton and the irreplaceable way of playing he represents.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: What about working with Milt Hinton?

Milt’s the greatest. You know, I mean we all love him, he’s going to be 85, but we’re also worried because when Milt goes, a sizable amount of this music goes, you know, a whole way of playing – a whole way of playing. There’s nobody else does that like that. So we

all guard him very dearly. It’s a whole feeling. It’s like the previous question, you can’t really write down what that feeling means. It’s, you just have to be there and be around the man and play, and feel the enthusiasm and how gets from one place to another. And I’ve tried to analyze it and find it very difficult.
